results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 59 aligned outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their spec paragraphs in spec order (p01-p60, including the declared trade-offs/verticals before in-practice order); the five callout units are unaligned framing, as expected.
The outliner marked no unit as having two ideas.
Every paragraph ties to S1-S6; the Bundeskartellamt bullet is the loosest but ends by tying dealer portability to integration principals (S4).

Tables and figures carry lead-ins or follow-up sentences that state what they show (e.g. 'As the table shows, a franchise network is a display and commercial concept...', 'Only the third survives staff turnover...'); documented-pattern bullets each end with what they show.

Each section opens with a bridge expressing the declared relationship ('Separating the advertiser's jobs starts with words', 'The three choices hold in every vertical; their weight shifts', 'Preventing these failures takes group decisions'); both flow readers confirm the bridges hold.

results.quote: Staff come and go, so listings belong to the organization and are assigned to branches.
results.finding: The KEY POINTS say organizations own listings, while the body, trade-off table and Failure Mode 1 say the seller account owns them; since the chapter distinguishes an organization (legal entity) from its per-brand seller accounts, both readers stopped to work out which owns listings.

results.quote: An **organization** is a legal entity that sells: a company, a sole trader's business, a public body.
results.finding: The trader entity is defined as 'organization' in Concepts but named 'Legal entity' in the entity table, Figure 3 and Decision 1, and membership is defined against an organization with no Organization row; both readers had to check the two names meant one entity.

results.quote: When Veldmark ID rolls out in 2028, the same identity gives her a separate Motorvane profile if she ever sells a car, but no Motorvane seller account until she creates one.
results.finding: The difference between a Motorvane 'profile' and a 'seller account' is not set up anywhere; storefront/profile was defined as a seller's public identity, so both readers re-read to see what she gets automatically.

results.quote: verified against the commercial register when it signed its contract in 2019, which until Motorvane's June 2027 re-check pilot was the only check Motorvane ran on dealers ([[identity-and-verification]]).
results.finding: The tangled relative clause and the unintroduced re-check pilot made both readers re-read to separate the 2019 check, the pilot and the target model.

results.draft_locus: In Practice, Documented patterns, Bundeskartellamt bullet
results.quote: its main stated reasons for clearance were Carwow's new-car focus and competition from AutoScout24
results.finding: The bullet spends most of its length on clearance reasons that do not bear on the account model; the link to integration principals arrives only in the last sentence, so both readers read it as a tangent.

results.quote: Keybridge reads and writes verification facts but nothing else.
results.finding: Keybridge was earlier described as having no link to anything else in the group by design; here it writes to the group registry without saying why a SaaS CRM writes verification facts. One reader re-read it.

results.quote: Where ratings attach is a modeling decision with legal weight; the branch, with a labeled network aggregate, is the safe default:
results.finding: The 'legal weight' promised is not what the following legal paragraph delivers (that paragraph is about disclosing how reviews are checked, not where ratings attach); one reader could not connect the opening sentence and the closing paragraph.
The table cites Rightmove's feed before the chapter has described it (only in In Practice), reading as a reference to something not yet seen. One reader, minor.

Every does_not_know term is explained at first use: trader and DSA trader traceability (Concepts), P2B, DAC7 and INFORM (regulation table), KYB and DMS (glossed inline), integration principal, branch, network, storefront (Concepts), ARPA (In Practice). Terms the flow readers flagged (Veldmark ID, Safe Deal, brand names, cast, Ghost Inventory) are on audience.already_knows.
Opens with the intriguing example of what 'seller' means in each vertical, bridges from the reader's own stretched user table, states the thesis and gives a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.
No 'in conclusion', no new subtopic or evidence; it answers the letter, completes the Part II test, names the 2027 decisions and hands off to Part III.

Synthesis no section states: one record answering four questions caused all four complaints, and with the seller account every reference the listing holds now has an owner, version and contract; so-what: 'Every later stage now reads a contract instead of copying a table.'

Returns to Agence Rhône Habitat's letter ('Each problem in Agence Rhône Habitat's letter now lands on its own entity') and to the Part II test ('name its owner, its version and the systems that copy it').
The cold reader predicted the sections in order, the evidence (Veldmark cases, public company documents, EU consumer, DSA and tax law) and the declarative practitioner tone.

Reader's prediction matches expected: scene at Hearthly, vocabulary of supply, model with lifecycle/lead routing/ratings, trade-offs and verticals, documented patterns and Femke/Ruhrblick/Poland, group sharing, failure modes, Chief Architect's decisions and questions; evidence from EU law, public company documents and fictional Veldmark.

Reader names the single cause (one advertiser record as login, legal identity, billing party, public profile and listing owner) and assigns each fact: franchisee legal entities as traders, reviews at branch, listings owned by the account and assigned to the branch with branch lead routing, separate contracts per franchisee, and Keybridge as an integration principal with scoped grants.

Reader lists the checkbox's lacks and legal dependencies (consumer law, DSA, DAC7), the four-part record with history, and the reclassification process (signals open a case, seller confirms or explains, outcome changes status/display/obligations and is recorded).

Reader explains indistinguishability, no throttling/per-dealer revocation, breakage on password reset and RFC 9700's ban on the password grant, and designs one client (client credentials or mTLS) with per-account, per-branch, scoped grants with dealer consent, individually revocable.

Reader shares login and the registry of public-register/verification facts, excludes packages, prices, leads and listing counts, links brand accounts only to registry entries, makes the cross-brand question a privileged report not an API, logs and reviews every use, and limits the agent software to an integration principal.
